components.name: Hooks
components.introduction: React hooks for local state, synchronization, and loading Solution data.
components.guidance: Use controlled state for local interaction. Effects should synchronize with external systems, not duplicate derived state.

members.name: useState(initial)
members.description: Returns the current state and a setter. Pass a value or an initializer function; updates can use the previous state.

members.name: useEffect(effect, dependencies)
members.description: Synchronizes with external systems after rendering. Return a cleanup function to release timers or subscriptions. Include every reactive value used by the effect in its dependencies.

members.name: useMemo(factory, dependencies)
members.description: Caches a calculated value until its dependencies change. Use it for expensive calculations, not required application state.

members.name: useRef(initial)
members.description: Returns a stable object with a mutable current property. Changing current does not trigger a render.

members.name: useApi(path)
members.description: Returns Solution data and an awaitable invalidator scoped to the full request path. The renderer handles initial loading, errors, and retry.

members.name: useConfirm()
members.description: Returns show(options), hide(), isOpen, and element; render element once in JSX. Options require title, actionLabel, and onAction: () => void | Promise<void>. Optional description, cancelLabel (default Cancel), and actionVariant: default | destructive (default default). Cancel receives initial focus; Escape cancels and backdrop clicks do not dismiss. Async actions show loading, prevent duplicate submissions, and close only after success. Failure keeps the dialog open for retry; scoped request errors are reported by the host, other errors appear inside the dialog. While pending, Cancel, Escape, show(), and hide() are ignored. Example: const confirmation = useConfirm(); confirmation.show({ title: 'Conferma variante A', cancelLabel: 'Annulla', actionLabel: 'Continua', onAction: async () => { await request('/api/variants', { method: 'POST', json: { variant: 'A' } }); } }); Render {confirmation.element} beside the trigger Button.

components.justification: Exposes React hooks and scoped Solution data-loading capabilities to isolated Views.

groups.Runtime: Local state, Solution data, requests, and scoped navigation.
groups.Action: Operations and navigation through buttons, links, and action menus.
groups.Display: Records, text, metadata, status, progress, and file previews.
groups.Form: Collecting and submitting input through forms and field components.
groups.Charts: Visualizing trends, category comparisons, part-to-whole breakdowns, and directed flows.
groups.Others: Additional interface components, including geographic maps.
groups.Layouts: Arranging content, panels, navigation, dialogs, tabs, and steps.

patterns.name: Confirmation
patterns.description: Ask for Continue or Cancel before a scoped Solution operation, without managing dialog-open state.
steps: Call useConfirm() at the top level and render its element once beside the trigger Button.
Call show({ title, actionLabel, cancelLabel, onAction }) from the trigger. Description is optional; use translated labels when needed.
Await request(path, { method: 'POST', json: payload }) inside onAction. Successful actions dismiss automatically; failures stay open for retry.

patterns.name: Data table
patterns.description: Present searchable records using data-driven rows and explicit query state.
steps: Load records with the documented Hooks API and keep search/filter state local.
Define Table columns and row actions using supported props; apply filtering or pagination on the server when needed.
Compose Empty with EmptyHeader and EmptyTitle when there are no matching records.

patterns.name: Editing form
patterns.description: Collect intent through named fields and persist changes through a validated Solution route.
steps: Inspect Form's submission contract and initialize fields from the record being edited.
Choose field components that match the server schema and use documented names and value contracts.
Submit to a Solution route that validates input and enforces authorization; display its documented success or error state.

patterns.name: Approval queue
patterns.description: Show pending work and make the next authorized action clear.
steps: Load pending records with the documented Hooks API and display their states as Table rows with Badge values.
Add explicit approve/reject actions through Button callbacks and scoped requests.
Enforce transitions and permissions on the Solution server, then refresh the queue after a successful action.
